properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From the dev_storyflow agent session of 2026-09-27 (art:dev-storyflow-feedback-2026-09-27, wish #48), written while the project moved to flo2.io and dev_storyflow was archived. Triaged 2026-09-28 on Anthony's word. The reporter's words: "a structured `repo` on artifact paths (or a relocation map the server resolves) would let a reader follow a citation without knowing the history". Wish #48: "A repository qualifier on artifact/path citations, or a server-side relocation map for an archived repo." The cause is fact:root-cause-a-location-is-anchored-to-a-root-the-design-never-records-2026-09-28.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) THE REPORTER'S FIRST: a structured repository qualifier on each artifact path (a `repo` beside `location`, or a `repo:path` form). Each citation is self-describing, and an archive is one fact about one repository. ⚠️ Counter: it scatters the same repository name across every artifact, which is the objection dec:idea-a-design-apart-from-its-code-knows-where-its-implementation-is raised against its own option (a).
(b) THE REPORTER'S SECOND: a server-side relocation map for an archived repository ("dev_storyflow/* now lives at …"), which the server resolves when a citation is read. Cheap to add after the fact, and it touches no existing node. ⚠️ Counter: it is a second record of what the location should have said, and a lookup table nothing checks goes stale. It also presumes the design knows which repository a path was in, and today it does not.
(c) FROM THE EARLIER IDEA, option (b) there: the design names each implementation (repository) ONCE, and a location is a path inside a named implementation. Where that repository is checked out, or that it is archived and where it went, is one fact on one node. This is (a) and (b) combined, but it needs req:the-design-knows-where-each-implementation-is built first.

THE HONEST COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, beside all three:
· MOST CITATIONS ARE PROSE. In reflow2's own design, 1,682 relative path citations sit in the statement text of 1,130 non-Artifact nodes, against 471 structured artifact locations. Of all those nodes, 7 name a repository in a path. A field on Artifact reaches the minority. The prose half needs either citations by artifact id or an accepted convention for writing the repository into the text, and neither is a schema change.
· AN ARCHIVE IS RARE, AND A MOVE IS NOT. The measured harm is broader than archiving: exporting a design and importing it into another folder re-anchored `docs/note.md` and reported the unchanged file missing_artifact. Any answer should cover a design moving to a server (the combined plan's position 11 moves flo2's and reflow2's own designs), not only a repository being archived.
· WHERE .reflow2.toml (#609) FITS: the pointer is code → design. It names designs, and `[[also]]` other designs with roles, never repositories, so it answers the reverse question. Option (c) would be its mirror image on the design side, and the two could be checked against each other, as dec:idea-a-checkout-knows-which-remote-design-it-implements already suggests.

A RANKING IS A FINDING, NOT A DECISION: (c) answers both wishes with one fact per repository, but it waits on a requirement nobody has scheduled. (b) is the only option that helps the already-archived dev_storyflow citations without rewriting them.
properties.name: OPEN — should an artifact or path citation carry a repository qualifier, or should the server hold a relocation map for an archived repository, so a reader can follow a citation without knowing the history?
properties.rationale: Recorded open because the need is already accepted as intent (dec:idea-a-design-apart-from-its-code-knows-where-its-implementation-is, kept 2026-09-25) while its mechanism is not. This report is the first field case of a repository going away, and it adds a measured fact: most citations are prose. The choice is Anthony's. Idea: the dev_storyflow agent session of 2026-09-27. Option (c), the counts and the counter-arguments: Claude Code, during the triage.
